inherited_register_metadata.counterfindings:
**Earlier criticisms that our own investigation narrowed or rejected**

These qualifications belong with the inventory:

- **“NIST denied free fall” is not an accurate description of its final account.** The final treatment recognizes the approximately 2.25-second interval; the remaining question is its mechanical reproduction, preserved in item 67. The draft-to-final history must not be used to erase the final acknowledgment. Source: [NIST FAQ, question 32](https://www.nist.gov/world-trade-center-investigation/study-faqs/wtc-7-investigation).
- **“A36 and A572 were modeled identically” is contradicted for the examined released upper-floor definitions.** The [October 24 material check](SOURCE-EXCERPTS.md#source-grades) compares their complete curves and finds distinct values. The pinned printed-table duplication remains a publication issue, while this result positively supports a publication-error explanation for those definitions. Historical invocation, effective assignments, physical grade validity, and version equivalence are not established; do not retain a claim that these grade-specific definitions are unavailable.
- **“No sensitivity studies existed” is unsupported.** The [structural audit, SC10](SOURCE-LINKS.md#ref-665a18b75415c247) records the 3.5-hour non-collapse control and prescribed-removal cases; the published account also compares debris/no-debris variants. The unresolved issue is adequacy, coverage, and reproducibility, not complete absence.
- **“All temperatures were inflated” is not established.** Repeated coefficients, fire-timing discrepancies, and uncertain inputs do not demonstrate a uniformly upward temperature error. Establish effective solver values, their derivation, and consequences before asserting bias. See items 14–19 and 69–71.
- **“No potentially relevant steel was examined or received” would erase affirmative evidence.** The Sample 1 examination, candidate inventory, and NIST receipt findings must remain alongside their unresolved attribution and custody limits; see revised item 59 and the [physical-documentary review](SOURCE-EXCERPTS.md#source-physical).
- **“Every discretionary modeling choice encouraged collapse” is not supported.** Capacity-enhancing assumptions and formulation-dependent fracture effects are contrary evidence; see items 78, 82, and 88. Their existence also does not prove the model historically accurate.
- **“NIST omitted all residual support” is unsupported.** The reviewed models include bearing, contact, discrete resistance, and retained supports.
- **Suspected connection-table ratio errors were not substantiated after allowing for display rounding.**
- **The seat-dimension erratum does not establish that the simulation used the erroneous printed dimension.**
- **Our proposed seamless join between two CBS clips failed.** It cannot support a continuous fire-duration measurement.
- **Our image work has not produced a defensible burning-window percentage or demonstrated temperature inflation.**
- **UAF’s prescribed broad support failures do not identify the historical cause of those failures.**
- **Other fire-driven pathways remain possible.** Weakening NIST’s exact sequence would not eliminate the entire fire-mechanism family.
- **Near-free-fall façade motion does not by itself identify initiation, whole-building force balance, or intent.**
- **No reviewed anomaly establishes an executed conspiracy or deliberate falsification.**

The strongest objection to treating this as a list of demonstrated failures is that **many entries identify what our available record cannot yet resolve**. Missing replication is weaker evidence than a reproduced contradiction. The highest-value next evidence remains the exact executed runs, paired sensitivity cases, processing histories, and independently testable output—not another accumulation of unexplained-looking details.

FEMA published a real metallurgical examination of Sample 1 with tentative WTC 7 attribution. The official inventory names four WTC7-labeled components within three numbered items, and the later NIST crosswalk supports receipt of A/W14A and B/W14B as unidentified sections. Their building/member attribution, any link to Sample 1, original location, alteration timing, and structural significance remain unresolved; C12a/b receipt also remains unresolved. These affirmative findings and limits are recorded in the [physical-documentary review](SOURCE-EXCERPTS.md#source-physical). They do not establish a pre-collapse intervention, a complete custody chain, or deception.

entries.title: Does the proposed lower-floor fire sequence reproduce the upper-façade free-fall interval?
entries.status: Inherited research observation or question; read its explicit limits
entries.original_record:
67. **Does the proposed lower-floor fire sequence reproduce the upper-façade free-fall interval?** NIST identifies the sustained uncontrolled fires on Floors 7–9 and 11–13, including Floor 13, while acknowledging approximately 2.25 seconds of essentially free-fall descent of the north face. This spatial separation makes the propagation and loss-of-support sequence a specific quantitative question. It does not establish a contradiction merely because the descending upper structure was above the principal fire floors.

    **The question to preserve:** Does NIST’s specified lower-floor fire damage and ensuing failure sequence actually produce sufficiently extensive loss of support, with the timing and residual forces necessary to reproduce the observed upper-façade acceleration, coherence, and motion? Relevant tests include matched model displacement/acceleration, member-force and contact histories, the failure chronology, and measurement and model uncertainty. This makes explicit the connection implicit in item 9 and historical inventory item 58.

    **NIST’s explanation and the mechanical qualification:** Upper stories need not themselves be heated to descend near gravitational acceleration if their supports fail below them. NIST attributes the interval to negligible support after lower exterior-column buckling. Compatibility with that explanation in principle does not independently validate its particular historical sequence; describing the process as progressive collapse does not replace the quantitative comparison.

    **Force constraint and observation limit:** For a defined fixed-mass body, sustained center-of-mass acceleration near gravitational acceleration requires a correspondingly small net non-gravitational vertical force. Substantial upward resistance cannot coexist with that motion unless physically justified downward forces offset it. A tracked roof point is not automatically that body’s center of mass. The body, interval, relative motion, projection, and uncertainty must be established or bounded. This limitation must be tested, not used to invent unlimited hidden motion or unexplained cancelling forces. The linked project force calculations are conditional analyses of separately identified published motion data, not an independent reproduction of NIST’s exact 2.25-second measurement or a measured historical force history. Neither the spatial separation nor free fall alone establishes simultaneous failure of every column, deliberate intervention, or a conspiracy.

    Sources: [NIST FAQ, questions 8–9 and 32](https://www.nist.gov/world-trade-center-investigation/study-faqs/wtc-7-investigation); [finite-interval force analysis](https://github.com/AveLyra/911-conspiracy-investigation/blob/b016bd3bf61bc664eb8b69d3e4b1828646c91fcc/investigation/wtc7/finite-interval-force/report.md); [roof-point and center-of-mass identifiability analysis](https://github.com/AveLyra/911-conspiracy-investigation/blob/b016bd3bf61bc664eb8b69d3e4b1828646c91fcc/investigation/wtc7/body-com-identifiability/report.md).

entries.title: Screenwall and west-penthouse ordering differs in the published comparison
entries.status: Inherited research observation or question; read its explicit limits
entries.original_record: 68. **Screenwall and west-penthouse ordering differs in the published comparison.** **AUDIT; matched-event verification remains.** The observation column places the east end of the screenwall below the roofline at 8.5 seconds and the west penthouse at 9.3 seconds; the debris-damage model lists 7.3/7.7 and 6.9/7.3 respectively, reversing their order in the paired views. A uniform clock shift cannot repair a reversal. The paired values represent viewpoints, not uncertainty intervals; feature definitions, sightlines, and occlusion must be matched before a stronger physical conclusion. Source: [common-observable source notes, NCSTAR 1A Table 3-1](https://github.com/AveLyra/911-conspiracy-investigation/blob/b016bd3bf61bc664eb8b69d3e4b1828646c91fcc/investigation/wtc7/common-observable-crosswalk/root-notes.md); [NIST authors’ paper, Table 1](https://tsapps.nist.gov/publication/get_pdf.cfm?pub_id=902588). entries.title: Fire-input uncertainty and the limits of the shifted-floor criticism need separate treatment
entries.status: Inherited research observation or question; read its explicit limits
entries.original_record: 69. **Fire-input uncertainty and the limits of the shifted-floor criticism need separate treatment.** **AUDIT; TEST/VERIFY for consequences and individual inputs.** The [floor-shift compatibility review](SOURCE-LINKS.md#ref-18edc4f7aa719a46) develops particular fire-spread/burning-duration comparisons but also limits the inference: sparse observations do not by themselves reject the applied thermal shift. Fuel distribution, door states, ventilation, and estimated photograph times remain inputs to check against the exact reconstruction. An apparent fire-timing difference is not a measured member-temperature error, and imagery does not supply the missing thermal history. Sources also include the [causal-chain synthesis](https://github.com/AveLyra/911-conspiracy-investigation/blob/b016bd3bf61bc664eb8b69d3e4b1828646c91fcc/investigation/wtc7/causal-chain-synthesis/report.md). entries.original_record: 82. **Later fracture research provides a concrete reason to test temperature-independent failure strain.** **AUDIT of the October 24 source review; applicability TEST unresolved.** The [fracture-temperature review](SOURCE-LINKS.md#ref-e8a4a5e9e198fa36) reports temperature-varying coupon fracture targets and mesh-/formulation-dependent calibrated erosion parameters in [Seif et al., Structures 6 (2016), 134–145, official NIST PDF](https://tsapps.nist.gov/publication/get_pdf.cfm?pub_id=919460). This is stronger than simply finding no validation record. It does not supply parameters that can be transplanted into the earlier coarse WTC 7 model, independently validate the whole sequence, or establish fabricated results. Reported engineering endpoint strain and local erosion strain are different quantities; the review shows that a constant cutoff’s direction of effect is not uniformly collapse-promoting. Historical material/part, formulation, run, and uncertainty joins remain missing. Related: item 35; supplied item 26.

entries.title: Witness and seismic observations need source-specific timing and attribution
entries.status: Exact-source or applicability check still open
entries.original_record: 86. **Witness and seismic observations need source-specific timing and attribution.** **VERIFY; no substantive local seismic audit located in this reconciliation.** The supplied inventory points to [NIST Response 2020-001, sections F–G](https://www.ae911truth.org/images/PDFs/NIST-Response-2020-001.pdf) for caution concerning weak seismic signals. Preserve that as an attributed source lead until its exact language, signals, station timing, localization, and model dependence are checked. Bangs and small seismic events cannot be uniquely classified as explosions or floor failures merely by association. Weak or ambiguous signals do not prove silence, and an untested intervention is not thereby supported. Conversely, the detection-analysis limits do not erase all negative evidence against conspicuously loud scenarios: an actual absence of a predicted signal can retain conditional weight where the recording coverage and source-to-receiver applicability support detection. The [acoustic audit](https://github.com/AveLyra/911-conspiracy-investigation/blob/b016bd3bf61bc664eb8b69d3e4b1828646c91fcc/investigation/wtc7/nist-acoustic-detectability/report.md) preserves that counterweight without claiming exclusion of every mechanism. Related: items 55–58; supplied items 39–40.

entries.title: End-to-end historical validation is distinct from component, solver, and comparator agreement
entries.status: Qualification / methodological boundary
entries.original_record: 87. **End-to-end historical validation is distinct from component, solver, and comparator agreement.** **Methodological qualification; TEST unresolved.** Component experiments, a fitted reduced model, solver agreement, another building fire, and comparison with WTC 7 observations support different propositions. None alone verifies the full independently justified heating → connection failure → propagation → observed-motion chain. Historical rarity is not a probability estimate or a demonstration of impossibility. Preserve empirical successes and negative controls alongside gaps, without converting them into either complete validation or complete absence of evidence. Sources: [connection audit](https://github.com/AveLyra/911-conspiracy-investigation/blob/b016bd3bf61bc664eb8b69d3e4b1828646c91fcc/investigation/wtc7/connection-calibration-audit/report.md), [original-experiment review](https://github.com/AveLyra/911-conspiracy-investigation/blob/b016bd3bf61bc664eb8b69d3e4b1828646c91fcc/investigation/wtc7/assembly-test-source-audit/report.md), and [causal-chain synthesis](https://github.com/AveLyra/911-conspiracy-investigation/blob/b016bd3bf61bc664eb8b69d3e4b1828646c91fcc/investigation/wtc7/causal-chain-synthesis/report.md). entries.status: Qualification / methodological boundary
entries.original_record: 88. **Conservative modeling and historical accuracy answer different questions.** **Methodological qualification; direction and magnitude require TEST.** A choice described as conservative must identify the response, comparison, and direction for which it is conservative; that label alone does not establish fidelity to this event or justify ignoring the choice. Conversely, not every approximation weakens the model: the [connection audit’s capacity discussion](https://github.com/AveLyra/911-conspiracy-investigation/blob/b016bd3bf61bc664eb8b69d3e4b1828646c91fcc/investigation/wtc7/connection-calibration-audit/report.md) records strength-enhancing assumptions as well as omitted mechanisms. The [fracture review](SOURCE-LINKS.md#ref-e8a4a5e9e198fa36) likewise limits claims of a uniform collapse-promoting bias. Preserve both directions in a matched sensitivity analysis. This records the supplied introduction’s conservative-modeling versus historical-accuracy distinction, not another independent observation against fire.

locators.excerpt:
NCSTAR 1-9 printed p. 568 / physical p. 634 describes the earlier-damage control as **4.0-hour temperatures with 3.5-hour ANSYS damage**, not a complete independent 3.5-hour temperature-and-damage history. The companion [NCSTAR 1-9A Section 4.4](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/Legacy/NCSTAR/ncstar1-9a.pdf#page=156), printed p. 105 / physical p. 156, states that this control was terminated because it had stabilized and no initiating event developed:

| Published calculation-clock item | Seconds |
| --- | --- |
| ANSYS damage application in these debris-damage cases | 8.5 |
| End of the 3.5-hour-damage control | 12.76 |
| Elapsed post-damage followup in that control | 4.26 |
| First Column 79 buckling in the 4.0-hour-damage case, Section 4.3.2 | 14.7 |
| Elapsed post-damage time to that buckling | 6.2 |

Thus the control's stated followup is **1.94 simulation seconds shorter** than the interval to first Column 79 buckling in the higher-damage case. These are solver clocks, not east-penthouse-aligned observation times.

This qualifies a broad statement that the two runs establish a sharp physical threshold. It does not show the control would collapse later. A stabilized lower-damage structure need not wait as long as a collapsing higher-damage structure; elapsed time alone does not invalidate the reported stopping decision. Independent assessment needs the control's full displacement/velocity and kinetic/internal-energy histories, stopping/damping settings, stability criteria, and an extended equal-horizon check. NIST's stated stability finding remains beside, not replaced by, the duration comparison.

locators.excerpt:
# UAF G3005 section verification and implications

October 21, 2026. **The available checked files do not establish whether UAF actually modeled G3005 as W21x44 or W24x55 in Figure 3.14.** The W21 caption and rendered annotation, the underlying W24 raster label, and NIST's separate W24 figure labels remain preserved. No native section was inferred from an annotation and no collapse model was run.

G3005 is a **floor beam**, not the Column 79 girder A2001. NIST's Figure 8-22 separately labels that girder W33x130. This distinction matters: uncertainty about one adjoining beam does not, by itself, establish the girder's section or invalidate every Column 79 result.

## Available file checks

The Intel operational-store identity passed. The public Git tree at `a1979eb700276e13e46e67cceff6a0954a55a649` contains 62,740 tracked paths and no candidate ending in the declared ABAQUS/SAP/native suffixes. The expanded, ignore-inclusive physical inventories also found no such standalone candidate:

| Physical research scope | File paths enumerated |
| --- | ---: |
| Active public checkout research directory | 45 |
| Active public checkout investigation directory | 281 |
| Intel operational public research tree | 39,037 |
| Current local Sherlock research tree | 4,364 |
| Retained Sherlock preservation tree | 10,034 |
| Intel operational Sherlock research tree | 9,046 |

These are overlapping storage snapshots, not counts of independent evidence. All six completed without enumeration errors. Exact roots, sorted path-list hashes and suffixes are recorded in [sources.json](https://github.com/AveLyra/911-conspiracy-investigation/blob/b016bd3bf61bc664eb8b69d3e4b1828646c91fcc/investigation/wtc7/uaf-g3005-native-section-2026-10-21/sources.json) and [observations.json](https://github.com/AveLyra/911-conspiracy-investigation/blob/b016bd3bf61bc664eb8b69d3e4b1828646c91fcc/investigation/wtc7/uaf-g3005-native-section-2026-10-21/observations.json). Symlink destinations and Git internals were not traversed. A small-plaintext native-keyword scan of the active public research/investigation checkout found no candidate. It did not search every historical Git blob, every possible extension, other disks, or proprietary embedded formats.

Five ZIP directories were inspected: the current and retained UAF wrappers, two Motion Lab archive copies and the compartment-data archive. None lists a member with a declared native suffix or a nested archive. The UAF copies are the same 834-byte, one-README wrapper, not the advertised model dataset. The other archives' directory checks do not authenticate their complete payloads; full-file SHA-256 was deliberately omitted for the two 172,774,879-byte copies. The named motion-score GZIP files were not decompressed. See [archive-directory-checks.json](https://github.com/AveLyra/911-conspiracy-investigation/blob/b016bd3bf61bc664eb8b69d3e4b1828646c91fcc/investigation/wtc7/uaf-g3005-native-section-2026-10-21/archive-directory-checks.json).

Neither UAF final PDF has an attached embedded file in its PDF embedded-file directory. Thus no hidden INP/CAE/ODB attachment was recovered from the reports. This does not exclude model information in another unexamined representation.

UAF's [official project page](https://ine.uaf.edu/wtc7) still advertises a 256 GB open-data download. That public-release claim and the checked local wrapper are different records. The wrapper refers to a repaired dataset corresponding to the September 2019 draft; the final-report case mapping remains unverified. This followup did not acquire the aggregate dataset or retry an inaccessible archive through another tool. Missing local inputs are not evidence that UAF never released models or that either party concealed them.

## Conflicting representations and case locators

Both preserved final PDFs retain the previously documented Figure 3.14 [PDF-layer discrepancy](https://github.com/AveLyra/911-conspiracy-investigation/blob/b016bd3bf61bc664eb8b69d3e4b1828646c91fcc/investigation/wtc7/c79-and-timing-crosschecks-2026-10-21/README.md):

| Source and location | Directly observed representation | What it does not establish |
| --- | --- | --- |
| UAF printed p. 86, physical p. 99, Figure 3.14 caption | W21x44 G3005 | Native geometry or assigned section |
| Same figure, visible vector annotation | `W21x44;  G3005 w/o bracing` | Native geometry or assigned section |
| Same figure, underlying embedded raster viewed separately in the preceding audit | `W24x55; G3005 w/o bracing` | Whether that label is stale or the actual input |
| NIST printed pp. 350 and 354, physical pp. 394 and 398, Figures 8-22 and 8-27 | Floor beams labeled W24x55 | The exact native assignment for the member called G3005, or assignments in later NIST models |

The whole rendered UAF page agrees with its caption; this is **not a visible caption-versus-plot-label disagreement**. Both versions have the same Figure 3.14 raster hash. This followup rechecked those hashes and the W21 text without altering either PDF. The preceding layer audit remains the source for the separate-raster manual transcription and covering vector rectangle.

Complete-page visual inspection identifies the braced Figure 3.11 on UAF printed p. 84 / physical p. 97 as `Model-9_Nonlinear_10s.odb`. Figure 3.14 names `Model-10_Nonlinear_10s_No_Support.odb`. The former locator had already appeared in the Figure 3.4 audit; this followup links it to the braced comparison as well. These are figure locators, not recovered files or proof that only bracing changed between the jobs. Both cases' section definitions are needed.

UAF printed p. 84 attributes W21x44 G3005 and four adjoining W24x55 beams to erection drawing E12/13. NIST's preliminary figures visibly group the floor beams under W24x55 labels. Consequently the UAF section criticism has a **publication-level basis**, independently of UAF's own Figure 3.14. Establishing an actual NIST modeling error still needs the member-specific native definition and applicable drawing/revision chain. The complete E12/13 original was not newly acquired or authenticated in this followup. The previously reviewed Column 79 shop details do not substitute for that floor-beam schedule.

## How the actual section could affect UAF criticism

| What native evidence eventually establishes | Consequence for this specific comparison |
| --- | --- |
| G3005 is W21x44 in the matching Figure 3.14 job | The W21 caption would be supported; a stale W24 raster annotation would remain a possible explanation, not an established editing history. The existing label conflict alone would not show a numerical-model defect. |
| G3005 is W24x55 in that job | The figure would not demonstrate the claimed W21x44 case. That would weaken its use as a quantitatively matched counterexample and require a correctly identified W21 comparison. It would not, by itself, refute the independently documented question about NIST's preliminary-model section. |
| The braced and unbraced jobs use different G3005 sections | Their difference could not be attributed solely to bracing. Section and bracing would need matched controls, even if each individual job ran correctly. |
| Native case or assignment remains unidentified | Both the section and its numerical effect remain unresolved; neither side gains a demonstrated physics result from the access gap. |

Changing a section can change axial and bending stiffness, torsional/warping response, local slenderness, thermal force transfer and the buckling sequence. A larger section can increase both restraint-generated force and resistance; the direction and magnitude of the resulting system effect are not determined from the designation alone. For illustration, free uniform thermal expansion is `alpha * deltaT * L`, whereas an ideal fully restrained elastic axial force is `E * A * alpha * deltaT`. These identities are not calculations of this heated composite floor or of lateral-torsional buckling. No numerical sensitivity or change in collapse outcome is claimed here.

The current causal comparison remains a **partial ordering, not a strict ranking
and not equal odds**. A newly acquired model file is not a new historical-cause
measurement. The warning is a model-quality concern, not a completed causal test.

| Requested category | Defensible ranking statement |
| --- | --- |
| Fire-driven collapse generally | Not ordered above or below specified deliberate removal by the current independent findings. |
| NIST's particular sequence | Nested within the fire family, not a separate competing cause. Developed and specifically challenged; its complete historical sequence is not established here. |
| Other fire-driven sequences | No specified substitute has earned a preferred position; possibility alone does not repair NIST's sequence. |

| Other/mixed mechanisms | Not ranked until sufficiently specified; not automatically last or assigned negligible probability. |

A subjective fire-first ordering could be constructed by adding a prior favoring
accidental failure over intervention; a removal-first ordering could be constructed

conditions. This investigation has not calibrated either decisive premise. Neither
is introduced here merely to satisfy a request for an ordinal list. The stronger
claim-level preference remains UAF's qualified criticism of NIST's demonstrated

locators.excerpt:
## What the original examination establishes

FEMA 403 Appendix C describes two examined members. Its introduction says Sample 1 appeared to originate in WTC 7; the section heading is more categorical. Its original location within the building was unknown. These are two separate attribution levels, and the heading cannot erase the introduction's qualification. The earlier 2001 JOM letter calls the beam WTC 7 material without that introductory qualifier, but likewise lacks an exact-location identification. These are overlapping reports by the same investigators, not independently authenticated recoveries.[1, C-1][2, opening paragraphs]

For Sample 1, the appendix reports near-surface oxidation and sulfidation, a eutectic reaction, grain-boundary penetration and substantial thinning. It identifies optical/scanning-electron metallography and qualitative energy-dispersive X-ray analysis; Figure C-8 ties spectra to selected regions. The authors infer local exposure approaching 1,000 °C from the microstructure and phase behavior. This is a retrospective local temperature inference, not an in-situ temperature record for the building or its load-bearing columns.[1, C-1 to C-5]

The distinction from Sample 2 matters. Sample 2 is associated with a tower, is described as copper-containing high-strength low-alloy steel, and has a different discussion of sulfides and possible melting. Its micrographs and temperature inference must not be relabeled as independent WTC 7 observations. The appendix's final discussion explicitly leaves the sulfur source, rate and pre-/post-collapse timing open.[1, C-5 to C-13]

The laboratory publication supplies positive evidence for the reported local alteration. It does **not** supply, in the inspected pages:

- A dated recovery photograph with an original-site location and uniquely linked member identifier.

locators.excerpt:
The examined records justify specific further inquiries, but do not establish a connection between a deliberate collapse operation and an identifiable person or physical specimen. They also do not justify dismissing the specimen or the handling problems as imaginary. The distinction is between an affirmative, bounded finding and the additional links needed to explain the collapse.

FEMA's published Sample 1 examination is positive evidence of a reported local metallurgical alteration. Its introduction tentatively attributes the member to WTC 7; its exact original location and the timing of the alteration remain unresolved in the examined record. The later abstract favoring post-collapse alteration is not a reproduced historical exposure. A critique's quotation about limited dissolution in a preliminary trial is a lead to original methods, not a substitute for them. See the [sample report](SOURCE-EXCERPTS.md#source-sample) and its [claim/lead ledger](SOURCE-LINKS.md#ref-2de31151fd026932).[1]

The DOJ OIG report documents souvenir-taking, inconsistent accounts of permission, management problems and a specific unforwarded communication. Those are affirmative handling concerns. The report also describes mixed building debris and expressly cannot establish that the investigated globe originated in WTC 7. Neither sorting in a WTC 7 area nor the existence of misconduct supplies a missing specimen-custody or mechanism-concealment link. See the [handling-records source audit](SOURCE-LINKS.md#ref-edc828d1b8f19311).[2]

No new evidence in this pass connects FEMA Sample 1 to the Fresh Kills operation. These are separate lead families until a record actually joins them.

locators.excerpt:
As of October 6, 2026, this research did not locate a publicly accessible final chemical analysis of the samples taken from the Urban Moving Systems van occupied by the five Israeli nationals detained in New Jersey on September 11, 2001. The released scans establish a canine alert, sample collection, and a September 23 report that the final results were pending. Later records establish administrative closure of laboratory leads, but do not identify the chemical finding.

**The supported conclusion is that the result remains unlocated in the public sources examined.** It is not established that the FBI never completed testing, never released a result to any requester, or obtained a positive or negative chemical result.

This investigation concerns the van bearing New Jersey registration JRJ13Y. It does not treat other vans, photography examinations, handwriting examinations, or intelligence trace checks as the same test. It is a research record, separate from the NIST litigation record and current pleading packet. No request, contact, filing, or transmission resulted from this research.

## What the released records establish

| Record | Location | Established fact | Limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| September 23, 2001 letterhead memorandum | Section 5, PDF pages 43–44; internal page 2 contains the sample paragraph | The van was searched by a trained dog; interior swabs were sent to the FBI laboratory; the memorandum says “Final results are still pending.” | This is a status statement on that date, not the later chemical result. |
| FD-192 evidence inventory | Section 1, PDF page 7; printed July 29, 2003; acquisition date September 12, 2001 | Newark retained fabric, blanket samples, and control swabs associated with JRJ13Y, with identifiable evidence barcodes. | Sample descriptions and barcodes are not laboratory findings. |
| Closing investigative package dated July 10, 2003 | Section 6, PDF pages 38–58; sample account at pages 42–43; administrative instruction at page 53 | The account still describes the dog alert and laboratory submission. Newark was instructed to discontinue outstanding CD-2C and Laboratory Division leads in ACS. | No chemical outcome is stated. The instruction does not distinguish completed examination, cancellation, or administrative closure. |
| Evidence retention memorandum dated April 14, 2004 | Section 6, PDF page 61 | Newark was awaiting a headquarters summary to determine final disposition of retained evidence after closing its inquiry. | This does not identify the disposition or chemical result of these samples. |
| Property memorandum dated February 18, 2005 | Section 6, PDF page 89 | After unanswered property-retrieval notices, the memorandum treats items as abandoned and states that they will be destroyed. | It is not a completed destruction certificate, does not identify the three sample barcodes, and does not establish destruction of a laboratory report. |

The September 23 date is visible on [the original scan of the memorandum](https://archive.org/details/DancingIsraelisFBIReport/fbi%20report%20section%205/page/n42/mode/1up); the pending-results sentence is on [the following page](https://archive.org/details/DancingIsraelisFBIReport/fbi%20report%20section%205/page/n43/mode/1up). The date and sentence no longer depend solely on the MintPress article’s attribution.

The later administrative instruction appears in [the July 2003 package](https://archive.org/details/DancingIsraelisFBIReport/fbi%20report%20section%206/page/n52/mode/1up). Its enclosed narrative [continues the sample-submission account](https://archive.org/details/DancingIsraelisFBIReport/fbi%20report%20section%206/page/n42/mode/1up) without stating a chemical result. The removal of the earlier pending-results sentence does not itself establish that testing was completed.

These are scans of apparent FBI records hosted by third parties, not files retrieved directly from an FBI production portal. Their official forms and internal consistency support their use, but the original agency production was not independently certified. Hash checks confirm the downloaded Internet Archive files match that archive’s metadata; they do not authenticate the archive against the FBI’s originals.

## The specific sample identifiers

The [FD-192 inventory](https://archive.org/details/DancingIsraelisFBIReport/fbi%20report%20section%201/page/n6/mode/1up) identifies property group **1B4**, the source vehicle **JRJ13Y**, and the owning office **Newark**.

| Item | Sample description | Evidence barcode |
|---|---|---|
| 15 | Fabric submitted as an explosives-residue sample | E01889035 |
| 16 and 17 | Control swabs from an agent’s gloves and bomb suits | E01889036 |
| 34 | Blanket samples collected for explosives-residue examination | E01889037 |

Item 35 is described as vacuuming and grouped with other property under E01889578. The visible inventory does not establish that it was part of the same chemical submission, so it is an additional lead rather than a confirmed laboratory specimen.

The glove and suit samples are explicitly controls. Counting these four item numbers as four confirmed explosives findings is unsupported. The phrase describing a sample’s intended examination also cannot substitute for a test result. The barcode is an evidence identifier; a laboratory accession number linking it to a completed examination remains unlocated.

Conversely, a project-completion or “former client” description by itself does not establish that every separately scoped maintenance duty, punch-list item, warranty obligation, credential, or permission ended. Those are open questions, not evidence that such access continued.

## Source observations, kept separate

1. **1997 issuer filing, accessed through a filing mirror.** Securacom’s September 1997 S-1/A describes an October 1996 $8.3 million contract “as part of” the WTC security upgrade and says several projects, including the WTC project, were expected to be substantially completed in 1997. That is a contemporaneous forecast about a defined project; it is not the contract, a completion certificate, or proof that all security work or access ended in 1997. The copy reviewed is hosted by SEC Info, not the SEC archive. [Securacom S-1/A filing copy](https://www.secinfo.com/dsvRq.834g.htm)

2. **2003 press account of company and filing descriptions.** An archived American Reporter article says Stratesec continued to list New York City’s World Trade Center as a “former client” through April 2001. It also attributes to CEO Barry McDaniel a description of an ongoing “completion contract,” reportedly “not quite completed when the Center went down.” The article does not reproduce the relevant contract, a statement of work, or the underlying filing pages in the copy reviewed. These are two attributed descriptions in one secondary source, not two independent confirmations. [Archived 2003 article](https://www.mail-archive.com/ctrl%40listserv.aol.com/msg102103.html)

3. **2005 retrospective reporting on the 1998 transition.** Margie Burns’s *Washington Spectator* article reports that the company received about $9.2 million from the WTC job from 1996 through 1998; it attributes to former manager Al Weinstein the account that Securacom was “excused from the project” in 1998 because it could not fulfill the work, and says EJ Electric took over the electronic-security work. This is a reporter’s account attributed to a former manager, not a termination notice, final invoice, or transfer/acceptance record. [Article copy](https://informationdissemination.org/archive/pdf/marvin.pdf)

4. **A separate former-employee account in that 2005 article.** The article says Jeff Gallup left Stratesec for Landtek and quotes him describing himself as “intimately involved” with WTC security until September 12, 2001; it reports that the FBI took the WTC visitor database from his office then. This is a claim about an individual’s involvement and the reported location of a database. It does not, by itself, establish that Stratesec still held the contract, that Gallup had WTC 7 access on September 11, or who owned or administered that database at the time.

## What changed

Across all six predefined window settings, both channels' highest-energy
candidate within the navigation region [12,14) seconds falls within
**[13.65,13.80) seconds of the excerpt**. This is an observed feature of the
preserved access-copy waveform. It gives a concrete provisional target for
subsequent perceptual annotation and source correspondence. It does **not**
identify that feature as the user's reported bang or as an explosive event.

The user's original rough marker remains 13 seconds, unchanged. The measured
interval above is the span containing the selected measurement bins, **not an
event onset, event duration, confidence interval or uncertainty bound**. Its
nominal compilation-track counterpart is [443.65,443.80); this arithmetic does
not establish original recording time, sound propagation or A/V synchronization.

All 17,006 channel-bin measurements and all 5,386 algorithmic candidate rows
agree across two independently implemented readers/calculators. Exact energy,
coordinates, peak indices and candidate identities match; largest RMS difference
is 5.56e-17, largest flank-ratio difference 8.89e-16. These are rounded-up error
bounds, not physical uncertainty. The full [comparison receipt](SOURCE-LINKS.md#ref-84eaf8f9219717f4)
retains exact maxima. The 5,386 rows are repeated numerical descriptions across
channels, scales and phases, **not 5,386 sounds or charges**.

## Declared sensitivity—not selection of one best trace

Displayed times are rounded to the shown decimals. These are highest-energy local-max candidates within the prospectively declared
[12,14) navigation interval. Equal-width exact energy orders RMS without its
rounding ambiguity. Every other candidate remains in the full output tables.

| Window | Phase in samples | Left candidate bin, local seconds | Right candidate bin, local seconds |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| 10 ms | 0 | [13.750,13.760) | [13.750,13.760) |
| 10 ms | 220 | [13.754989,13.764989) | [13.754989,13.764989) |
| 20 ms | 0 | [13.680,13.700) | [13.680,13.700) |
| 20 ms | 441 | [13.750,13.770) | [13.670,13.690) |
| 50 ms | 0 | [13.750,13.800) | [13.650,13.700) |
| 50 ms | 1102 | [13.674989,13.724989) | [13.674989,13.724989) |

For these twelve selected candidates, digital RMS is 1.59–2.66 times the RMS
in the preceding 0.25-second flank, and 1.36–2.26 times that in the following
flank (rounded ranges, not enclosing bounds). Those flanks are not established background-noise baselines. Ratios are
within the processed waveform, not sound-pressure or explosive-yield estimates.

The two-channel/scale disagreement is material: some settings prefer a portion
near 13.68 seconds and others near 13.76. The method does not merge these into
one event or choose a unique onset. In the full 25-second excerpt, the right
channel's highest-energy candidate is in this navigation region for all six
settings; the left channel's is later, in bins between 18.80 and 19.475 seconds.
Thus “the loudest peak in the file” would not uniquely select this feature even
under this restricted digital metric. Two channels are not two independent
microphone witnesses, and no new listening or speech classification was done.

## Methods and provenance

The [protocol](SOURCE-LINKS.md#ref-cd0602f335af70e8) was frozen before this unit's historical measurements.
Prior knowledge of the user's marker and earlier work is disclosed. The source
is the existing 25-second, 44.1-kHz, float32 stereo WAV, SHA256
`b8557ab9a0f2ac6dc9d3d59d0334de96431340ad34f2e5642c47a5a51a3a09dd`.
Both programs independently verified its hash/header and checked guarded source
bytes before and after computation. No new historical decode or recording
authentication is claimed. The [earlier source check](https://github.com/AveLyra/911-conspiracy-investigation/blob/b016bd3bf61bc664eb8b69d3e4b1828646c91fcc/investigation/wtc7/audio-listening-2026-10-05/source-check.md)
supplies recorded derivation lineage; the [observation table](SOURCE-LINKS.md#ref-0b7e1ca00b7c21dd)
preserves reports and source-test limits. Neither is another acoustic witness.

Each grid covers all samples exactly once, including flagged partial edge bins.
RMS includes DC; channels are never mixed. Candidates are every exact-energy
local-max plateau whose own bins and immediate neighbors are full-width. No
threshold, minimum separation or statistical/explosion detector is used.
Exact integer energy ordering prevents a tolerance-pass from hiding a different
discrete candidate decision. Partial/endpoint candidates are excluded by rule,
so these summaries are not a complete extrema inventory for arbitrary windows.

Root uses SciPy's WAV reader, NumPy float64 arithmetic, and IEEE-bit exact energy;
the separate implementation uses RIFF/struct parsing, math.fsum and integer-ratio
exact energy. Its author had not inspected root historical outputs before saving
its result. Shared PCM and protocol limit independence to parsing/arithmetic,
not source history or expert forensic interpretation. Full controls, code pins,

## Exact lead and why it matters

The preserved municipal catalog, one-based row3155, identifies first Bates
NYC-WTC_000174136 in WTC7 / 7DCAS, under the label Emergency Generator
Operation®Press Room®Audio Visual Work®Leak Detection System. The row reports
one document and one page; an individual byte count is not established.
Root checked the exact row and catalog hash. The separate readiness reader
located the same lead in the prior metadata review, outside both the111-record
and97-record returned batches and without a completed same-ID reading in the
bounded local paths it searched. This does not prove it was never reviewed
elsewhere or that the entire archive was searched.

The label is more specifically relevant than another generic fit-out list,
but could describe a request, coordination memo or unrelated operating issue.
It does not establish a date, equipment identity, successful test or closure.
The next content question is whether the item explicitly links to the March9
generator/ATS/fuel requests or the reported July31 test and its seven open items.

Importantly, the earlier [Job1854 report](https://github.com/AveLyra/911-conspiracy-investigation/blob/b016bd3bf61bc664eb8b69d3e4b1828646c91fcc/investigation/wtc7/municipal-originals-2026-10-04/generator-job1854/report.md)
already describes source assertions of actual July31 testing and present
emergency readiness alongside unfinished work. This is reliance on that prior
review, not a fresh reading of those PDFs. The missing issue is exact closure,
configuration and underlying corroboration, not whether any testing was ever
reported. The newly reviewed March punch list neither erases nor independently
confirms those later assertions.

## Actual attempt and stop

The [protocol](SOURCE-LINKS.md#ref-b710bfc9d10902da) and exact [request](SOURCE-LINKS.md#ref-b7eade3a41966b20) were saved
before one public HTTPS POST to the established NYC archive search endpoint.
It requested the eleven existing metadata fields, count10, and zero source
content sampling. The [attempt receipt](SOURCE-LINKS.md#ref-63fc80012f86e861) preserves the command,
clock qualification, terminal result and control hashes.

The request ended with curl exit28 after15.005907seconds, HTTP000, no supplied
content type, zero received bytes and zero redirects. The reported error was
a connection timeout. The terminal state was obtained by polling the same
live session28594; no restart occurred. An explicit filesystem check found no
response file or symlink. An absent file has no acquired-byte hash; none was
invented. No empty placeholder was created to resemble a source response.

Under the frozen protocol, metadata failure stops this route before the
conditional PDF request. There was no retry, alternate host, credential,
cookie, new query, neighboring ID or source-content inspection. HTTP000 is
not a server denial. This result establishes neither missing public records
nor withholding, concealment or the historical document's contents.

## UAF thermal expansion needs a case-specific baseline

UAF Section 2.1.3.4, printed p. 32 / physical p. 45, states a general constant steel coefficient of 14 microstrain/C, approximately 7.78 microstrain/F. Section 3.2.2, printed pp. 80-81 / physical pp. 93-94, describes an approximately 40-percent increase to 11.5 microstrain/F for named beams in the modified plate case.

**If** the Chapter 2 value was the baseline for that Chapter 3 case, the increase is about **47.8 percent**, using either stated temperature-unit system. The slight difference between 47.8149 percent and 47.8571 percent reflects which published rounded unit value is used; both calculations are recorded rather than collapsed into one exact input.

This is a conditional reporting ambiguity, not proof of a wrongly entered parameter. The Chapter 3 baseline may differ, and the word approximately limits the precision claimed. Its actual material definition has not been recovered. The [existing factorial protocol](https://github.com/AveLyra/911-conspiracy-investigation/blob/b016bd3bf61bc664eb8b69d3e4b1828646c91fcc/investigation/wtc7/c79-factorial-protocol-2026-10-19/README.md) retains its unknown baseline; it is not silently populated with either 7.78 or 11.5/1.4. The modified case already changes geometry and expansion together, so it remains unsuitable as an isolated measurement of the side plate's effect without the planned controls.

The MFR is dated April20,2004 and identifies Team1A and its preparer. It is a
staff memorandum of an interview, not a verbatim deposition transcript or audio
recording. Its six physical pages were read and visually inspected in full.

Physical4 records the following sequence: Bin Don and Bayoumi ordered food and
sat waiting; Hazmi and Mihdhar entered speaking Arabic; Bayoumi addressed them
and invited them to sit. It reports an invitation to San Diego, an apparent
telephone-number exchange whose precise sequence the witness could not recall,
and departure after about **thirty minutes**. It also records the witness's
emphatic denial of advance information about the meeting and description of it
as **purely a coincidence**. Both assistance-related observations and that
contrary interpretation remain together.

The MFR says his Arabic was **limited**, the exchange was vague to him, and
Bayoumi sometimes translated. This qualifies use of him as an independent
witness to the conversation's content. It does not permit either treating him

original_record.heading: BP01 — Conflicting reimbursement assessments
original_record.source_level: Published research entry; primary-source citations and limitations retained in its original body.
original_record.verbatim_published_body:
The declassified Joint Inquiry, **printed p.422, footnote 1; physical PDF p.13**, places
two FBI accounts alongside one another. Its quotation of a **November 18, 2002
response, p.3**, says an equal cash deposit on the check date suggests reimbursement.
Its quotation of an **October 14, 2002 document** says there was no bank
documentation supporting reimbursement from Hazmi or Mihdhar. We acquired the
congressional reproduction, not those two underlying FBI originals.
[Joint Inquiry release](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/GOVPUB-Y4_IN8_18-PURL-gpo71223/pdf/GOVPUB-Y4_IN8_18-PURL-gpo71223.pdf#page=13)

A **July 21, 2004 FBI EC**, **EO14040-002738; physical p.16**, describes a $1,558
cashier's check, an equal cash **deposit**, and the $9,900 account opening, all posted
within seven minutes on February 4, 2000. It reports teller corroboration; the
reference identifying the teller interview is redacted. This is the FBI's account
of the records and corroboration, not our independent bank/teller examination.
[FBI Part 5](https://vault.fbi.gov/9-11-attacks-investigation-and-related-materials/9-11-material-released-in-response-to-executive-order-14040/documents-responsive-to-executive-order-14040-2-c-part-5/at_download/file#page=16)

The OIG's same-day repayment account and the 2025 court's repayment finding remain
beside these records. Neither repetition supplies the missing transaction images.
The court cites **KSA Ex91, FBI2808–09**, not plaintiffs' Ex91 (Ratchford declaration).
[OIG chapter 5, notes128–129](https://oig.justice.gov/sites/default/files/archive/special/0506/chapter5.htm)
· [2025 opinion, p.21](https://www.nysd.uscourts.gov/sites/default/files/2025-08/03-md-01570%2011182.pdf#page=21)

**Open test:** obtain both dated FBI documents, the original credit/debit ledger,
cash deposit/check images and teller statement. Equal amounts alone do not identify
the person who supplied cash. No preferred account is selected here.

The released **August 4–6, 2003 Bayoumi interview FD-302**, transcribed August 18,
**continuation p.5, physical p.11, Bates000002669**, records his uncertain estimate
that the men possessed **$4,000–$8,000**. Later records describe a **$9,900 cash
opening deposit**. The original receipt identified as **plaintiffs Ex550/FBI8057**
has not been acquired here. The interview and reported receipt concern differently
described quantities and different levels of certainty; retain both without turning
the mismatch into a finding of lying.
[Released interview](https://vault.fbi.gov/9-11%20Commission%20Report/9-11-investigation-2003-09-sep/at_download/file#page=11)

A 2024 Motley Rice news account attributes nearly $10,000 transferred into their
account to Bayoumi. Its own public averment §1637 instead describes Mihdhar's cash
deposit; the court p.21 also attributes the cash deposit to the hijackers. These
descriptions are preserved, not equated. A bank companion, cash depositor and
ultimate source of funds are separate propositions.
[News account, extracted block B056](https://www.motleyrice.com/news/september-11-2001-new-evidence-23-years-later)
· [Averment §1637, physical p.416](https://www.motleyrice.com/sites/default/files/documents/AT_HR/9-11/20240802%20Redacted%20public%20averment.pdf#page=416)

**Open test:** receipt, account-opening documents and cash-origin evidence. The
$9,900 amount alone does not establish intent to evade reporting requirements.

described quantities and different levels of certainty; retain both without turning
the mismatch into a finding of lying.

A 2024 Motley Rice news account attributes nearly $10,000 transferred into their
account to Bayoumi. Its own public averment §1637 instead describes Mihdhar's cash
deposit; the court p.21 also attributes the cash deposit to the hijackers. These
descriptions are preserved, not equated. A bank companion, cash depositor and
ultimate source of funds are separate propositions.

**Open test:** receipt, account-opening documents and cash-origin evidence. The
$9,900 amount alone does not establish intent to evade reporting requirements.

original_record.heading: BP04 — A specific post-bank call sequence, with limited attribution
original_record.source_level: Published research entry; primary-source citations and limitations retained in its original body.
original_record.verbatim_published_body:
The **September 29, 2005 FBI telephone-analysis EC**, **EO14040-002752; physical p.30,
printed p.5**, places the bank visit approximately **15:30–15:40** and prints:

| Time as printed | From label | To label | Duration as printed |
|---|---|---|---|
|16:40|BAYOUMI Cell|AULAQI Home|1:00|
|16:42|BAYOUMI Cell|AR-RIBAT PAYPHONE|1:00|
|16:43|BAYOUMI Cell|AR-RIBAT FAX|1:00|
|16:52|ALTHUMAIRY (CBR)|BAYOUMI Cell|1:00|
|16:55|BAYOUMI Cell|ALTHUMAIRY (CBR)|2:00|

This is an original FBI **analysis table**, not the carrier return for those calls.
Its later discussion states that the calls' significance is unknown because their
content is unavailable. It also records Bayoumi's denial of introductions while
offering introductions as an investigative possibility.
[Table](https://vault.fbi.gov/9-11-attacks-investigation-and-related-materials/9-11-material-released-in-response-to-executive-order-14040/documents-responsive-to-executive-order-14040-2-c-part-5/at_download/file#page=30)
· [limits, EO14040-002759/p.37](https://vault.fbi.gov/9-11-attacks-investigation-and-related-materials/9-11-material-released-in-response-to-executive-order-14040/documents-responsive-to-executive-order-14040-2-c-part-5/at_download/file#page=37)

The averment §1639 calls the 16:55 destination Thumairy's **cell phone**; the FBI
table calls it **CBR**, and EO14040-002757 describes that number as a can-be-reached
number subscribed to someone else. Preserve both descriptions; the carrier and
subscriber evidence needed to map them is still missing. A fax/payphone label does
not identify a particular human speaker.
[Averment §1639/p.416](https://www.motleyrice.com/sites/default/files/documents/AT_HR/9-11/20240802%20Redacted%20public%20averment.pdf#page=416)
· [number definitions, FBI p.35](https://vault.fbi.gov/9-11-attacks-investigation-and-related-materials/9-11-material-released-in-response-to-executive-order-14040/documents-responsive-to-executive-order-14040-2-c-part-5/at_download/file#page=35)

**Open test:** plaintiffs Ex12A, Ex5 p.197 and their underlying Sprint/local-carrier
returns; mapping/subscriber documents, direction, timezone, billing units and
duplicate-record rules. Timing is a testable lead; conversational purpose is not
established by proximity to the bank visit.

original_record.heading: BP06 — Count rows, line sets and people separately
original_record.source_level: Published research entry; primary-source citations and limitations retained in its original body.
original_record.verbatim_published_body:
The FBI table **EO14040-002757–002759, physical pp.35–37** says **67 contacts** for
December 16, 1998–December 20, 2000. A reproducible extraction counts **67 printed dated
rows**. In the inclusive December 6, 1999–February 4, 2000 window it counts **27 rows**:
**21** involving BAYOUMI#2 and **6** involving BAYOUMI#4. The averment **§§1641–1643**
uses **22 calls** for that window. Both counts and the unsupplied selection rule
are preserved. No subset is asserted to explain the pleading's total.
[FBI table](https://vault.fbi.gov/9-11-attacks-investigation-and-related-materials/9-11-material-released-in-response-to-executive-order-14040/documents-responsive-to-executive-order-14040-2-c-part-5/at_download/file#page=35)
· [Averment §§1641–1643, physical pp.416–417](https://www.motleyrice.com/sites/default/files/documents/AT_HR/9-11/20240802%20Redacted%20public%20averment.pdf#page=416)

[CALL-ROWS.json](CALL-ROWS.json) preserves every printed row and its extracted-text
line; [recount_calls.py](recount_calls.py) reproduces the count from the pinned PDF.
Rows are not automatically unique conversations: matching two endpoints, repeated
entries and carrier billing conventions require checks. No statistical claim of
an unusually dense call cluster is made without comparable coverage and baseline.

KSA's public reply disputes shared-line attribution and the proposed call-circle
inference. Preserve this adversarial account alongside the plaintiffs' account;
neither is a carrier record. The 2025 court made substantive jurisdiction findings,
but reserved merits/credibility determinations; this review does not erase that.
[KSA reply, printed p.15/physical p.29 n.8](https://www.motleyrice.com/sites/default/files/documents/AT_HR/9-11/Docket%20%23%209795%20-%20Redacted%20Public%20Version%20%20KSA%20REPLY%20MOL%20ISO%20%5B9368%5D%20MTN%20to%20Dismiss%20%28Prev.%20filed%20under%20seal%20on%203.4%2C%202024%29.pdf#page=29)

original_record.heading: BP07 — The FBI's received-record windows are not full service histories
original_record.source_level: Published research entry; primary-source citations and limitations retained in its original body.
original_record.verbatim_published_body:
**EO14040-002749, physical p.27** lists seven line-specific toll-record ranges:

| FBI list item | Provider/line description | Tolls received cover |
|---|---|---|
|1|Pacific Bell home|Jan 17, 2000–Jun 30, 2001|
|2|Sprint cell, earlier number|Jan 9, 2000–Jun 7, 2000|
|3|Sprint cell, later number|Jun 8, 2000–Apr 2, 2001|
|4|Airtouch, c/o spouse|Nov 20, 1998–Sep 20, 2000|
|5|Pacific Bell Wireless, spouse subscriber|Sep 1, 2000–Jul 28, 2001|
|6|Pacific Bell mosque office|Jul 1, 1998–Apr 22, 2001|
|7|Pacific Bell, primarily Internet connection|Dec 15, 1999–Jan 17, 2001|

The earlier Sprint service is separately described as beginning September 27, 1998.
Its listed toll coverage begins much later. This does not establish that earlier
calls never happened, were destroyed, or were never collected elsewhere.
[Inventory](https://vault.fbi.gov/9-11-attacks-investigation-and-related-materials/9-11-material-released-in-response-to-executive-order-14040/documents-responsive-to-executive-order-14040-2-c-part-5/at_download/file#page=27)

**Open test:** provider return manifests, subpoena date/scope, all pages, import
logs and the relationship among changed numbers, office lines and subscriber/users.
Unobserved intervals must not be counted as zero calls.

original_record.heading: BP08 — An actual carrier-record sample and its custody trail
original_record.source_level: Published research entry; primary-source citations and limitations retained in its original body.
original_record.verbatim_published_body:
The FBI's **2(c)/2(d) supplemental release1** contains:

- **EO14040-003831; physical p.164:** January 7, 2002 FD-302 saying AT&T toll records
  were entered on December 27, 2001; it describes eight calls on June 23, 2000.
- **EO14040-003832; p.165:** data-loading request with originals-attached marked
  yes, assigned December 27 and completed December 28, 2001.
- **EO14040-003833; p.166:** AT&T November 29, 2001 subpoena-return letter describing
  **two accounts for one number**, enclosed account/toll material and an **18-month**
  retention period. This records the carrier's statement, not independent legal
  verification of its retention-law claim or proof about other carriers.
- **EO14040-003865 and003867; pp.198,200:** July 4, 2000 bill usage summary and actual
  carrier call-detail page: **eight June 23 rows, six to Saudi Arabia and two to the
  UK, total42 billed minutes**. This agrees with the FD-302's count/date/destination
  description. Recipient/account numbers are redacted and are not republished.
- **EO14040-003884; p.217:** a separate July 27, 1998 carrier call-detail page, showing
  that the public packet includes earlier original billing material too. It is not
  joined to the July 2000 account through redacted identifiers.

[Carrier return and loading trail](https://vault.fbi.gov/9-11-attacks-investigation-and-related-materials/9-11-material-released-in-response-to-executive-order-14040/documents-responsive-to-executive-order-14040-2-c-2-d-supplemental-release-1/at_download/file#page=164)
· [Original call detail](https://vault.fbi.gov/9-11-attacks-investigation-and-related-materials/9-11-material-released-in-response-to-executive-order-14040/documents-responsive-to-executive-order-14040-2-c-2-d-supplemental-release-1/at_download/file#page=200)

This is a positive source check within one evidentiary chain, not independent
corroboration by multiple witnesses. It does not authenticate the February 4
cellular sequence or identify the June 23 speakers. The carrier's bill legend says
one call can be displayed more than once for separate rate periods; that convention
must be checked before using row totals from this carrier as unique-call totals.
It is not assumed to explain the separate 27-versus22 comparison.

original_record.heading: BP09 — Payment originals and a specific custody concern
original_record.source_level: Published research entry; primary-source citations and limitations retained in its original body.
original_record.verbatim_published_body:
The **October 28, 2001 rental-manager interview**, transcribed October 29,
**EO14040-003828–003830; supplemental1 physical pp.161–163**, describes the check as
**$775 deposit + $8 insurance + $775 rent = $1,558**. The averment §1638 instead
describes rent, security deposit and an application fee. Keep both component labels.
The interview says Bayoumi brought the check **alone**; the averment §1638 describes
him returning with both men. We have not obtained the cited later declaration and
deposition needed to compare those accounts directly.
[Interview p.2](https://vault.fbi.gov/9-11-attacks-investigation-and-related-materials/9-11-material-released-in-response-to-executive-order-14040/documents-responsive-to-executive-order-14040-2-c-2-d-supplemental-release-1/at_download/file#page=162)
· [Averment §1638](https://www.motleyrice.com/sites/default/files/documents/AT_HR/9-11/20240802%20Redacted%20public%20averment.pdf#page=416)

The interview also reports a roughly February 15 **$1,010** cashier's check and says
its difference from the $775 rent was unexplained to the witness. The ledger,
receipt/check images, credits and allocation are needed; the difference is not
evidence of concealed funding by itself.

original_record.additional_context: CIA physical p.81 / printed p.56 reports a January20 note saying the FBI had been kept abreast. It expressly leaves CIA personnel accountability to CIA OIG. Preserve that adverse-to-misconduct finding with the performance criticisms; do not extend it to every CIA action.

original_record.title: Official notification accounts differ in flight identity as well as stated times
original_record.claim_type: Conflicting published official accounts
original_record.observation: The reproduced September18,2001 NORAD release and FAA table give AA77 notification09:24 and UA93N/A or NA. May23,2003 testimony gives UA93 possible-hijack notice09:16. The 2004 Commission account gives first NEADS UA93 notice10:07, AA77 missing09:34, and identifies the09:24 log entry as phantom AA11.

original_record.title: DOT reports executives knew a liaison answer was inaccurate and did not correct it
original_record.claim_type: Affirmative oversight finding of knowledge plus noncorrection
original_record.observation: The QFR claimed the Air Force liaison immediately joined the bridge after08:46. OIG says she joined only after09:37, that three executives learned the answer was inaccurate, and none corrected it with the Commission.
conflicting_or_qualifying_records: OIG distinguishes the executives’ later knowledge from their initial reliance on an erroneous chronology. Their reported assumptions about who would correct the answer conflict with the liaison’s account that no one asked her to do so.

The report finds an affirmative obligation to correct and recommends considering administrative action for two then-current executives. It does not document action actually taken, prove coordinated concealment, or connect this post-event failure to attack preparation.
FAA’s over6,000 documents/materials supplied to the Commission are stated as mitigation/context, not a reason to erase the knowledge/noncorrection finding.

original_record.title: Mineta and the Commission preserve incompatible early/later PEOC timing accounts
original_record.claim_type: Conflicting retrospective accounts; arithmetic only
original_record.observation: Mineta says he reached PEOC about09:20 and heard the exchange about five or six minutes later. The Commission describes Cheney’s conference-room arrival shortly before10:00, perhaps09:58, and different later inbound-aircraft exchanges at10:10–10:18.
conflicting_or_qualifying_records: About09:20 versus perhaps09:58 gives a nominal38-minute contrast; conditional09:25–09:26 versus10:10–10:18 allows a44–53-minute forward shift for interval overlap. These calculations do not measure clock error or establish that the two sources describe the same exchange.
The Commission acknowledges conflicting arrival evidence and no documentary evidence for an earlier claimed authorization call, while noting incomplete relevant sources.
Tunnel entry, shelter conference-room arrival and later order exchanges are distinct event types. No original PEOC logs, witness clock calibration or common-event join was authenticated.
original_record.next_test: Acquire PEOC Shelter/Watch/Communications/9-11 logs, White House switchboard records, witness notes and calibration evidence; test multiple-event as well as memory/clock alternatives.
